$comment: This file describes WHERE this service's logs end up, per environment, so that a
human or DevAgent can answer 'what is the active observability backend for prod?'
by reading one file instead of tracing shell scripts and Terraform.
IT IS NOT A RUNTIME CONFIGURATION. Nothing reads it at runtime, at deploy time, or
at build time. The actual pipeline is: the backend writes JSON lines to stdout,
systemd appends them to backend.log, the CloudWatch agent tails that file. Editing
this file changes no behaviour — it is documentation with a schema. Changing where
logs actually go means editing infra/scripts/provision-backend.sh and
infra/observability.tf, and then updating this file to match.
That separation is deliberate. An earlier draft had a registry that the deploy
script parsed to decide which exporters to build, which meant a documentation file
could break a deploy. Metadata should not be able to do that.
EXTENSIBILITY: `destinations` is an array so a second backend (Grafana Loki, an
OTLP collector, anything) can be listed alongside CloudWatch with enabled:false, and
DevAgent can highlight the active one, without the application's logging
implementation changing at all. The app only ever writes JSON to stdout.

pipeline.$comment: The actual, implemented path. Nothing else is implemented.
stages: application writes structured JSON (one object per line) to stdout
logrotate (copytruncate, 50M x 5) bounds the file on disk

authentication.$comment: No token, key, or secret exists anywhere in this path. The instance role grants logs:PutLogEvents on THIS environment's log group ARNs only (infra/observability.tf), so nonprod cannot write into prod's logs.

cost.notes: Retention is capped in Terraform rather than left at the CloudWatch default of never-expire, which is the usual cause of an unexpected bill. Logs Insights queries cost $0.005 per GB scanned.

destinations.$comment: Edge logs. Plain text, not JSON — nginx's default combined format.

prod.$comment: info, not debug: prod volume is the cost driver for CloudWatch ingest.

authentication.$comment: Separate role from nonprod, scoped to prod's log group ARNs only.

log_record_fields.$comment: The JSON fields on every backend record. These are what make a separate metrics system unnecessary — Logs Insights derives request rate, error counts and p99 latency from them. Queries are in OBSERVABILITY.md.

not_implemented.$comment: Listed so nobody — human or agent — builds a dashboard against something that does not exist. These are FUTURE CAPABILITIES, not current ones.
not_implemented.metrics: No /metrics endpoint, no CloudWatch custom metrics, no EMF. Use Logs Insights.
not_implemented.traces: trace_id/span_id are stamped on log records, but NO spans are exported. There is no X-Ray or tracing backend.
not_implemented.dashboards: None. No Grafana, no CloudWatch dashboards.
not_implemented.slos: No SLOs, error budgets, deploy watch, or incident management.
